text: IT COSTS MORE TO BE POOR / THE POOR TRAP / THE RICH HACK
scene: A vertical black line splits the frame. On the left a soot-smudged cartoon man in a navy suit grips a steering wheel beside a rusty brown car with flames at the hood, a grey smoke plume, flying green bills and cracked ground. On the right a clean man with round glasses and folded arms leans on a blue car that has tank-style tread wheels, with a translucent green shield glowing in front of the bonnet.
mechanism: A poor-versus-rich split where the burning wreck and the shielded car dramatise one idea, with the headline stating the claim and two sub-labels naming each side.
composition: Near-mirror two-panel layout with a top headline band, then two small sub-labels, then one figure and one car per side. The shield on the right is the largest single shape and the smoke plume pulls the left panel's eye to the edge. White space between figures keeps the halves separate, although the left half carries more small debris.
typography: Twelve words across three tiers: a wide black bold headline on one line, then two smaller sub-labels of three words each above the halves. The headline stays readable at 160x90 but the sub-labels shrink to thin strokes. The title mentions double and broke while the thumbnail adds the poor-versus-rich framing.
colors: Mostly white with navy suits, rust orange and brown on the wreck, and cool blue plus a pale green shield on the rich side. Warm orange flames against cool green gives each side a distinct colour identity; the grey smoke is the only desaturated mass.
psychology: The left man has droopy half-closed eyes, an open slack mouth and soot on his face and suit, while the right man has a slight closed-mouth smile and crossed arms. These contrasting poses and expressions set up a struggling-versus-secure story through cartoon cues only.
partnership: The title speaks of paying double for everything, and the thumbnail turns that into a vehicle-repair contrast without any price. The headline mostly restates the title idea, but the shield and tread car pose an unanswered question about what the hack is.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: black headline first, then the burning car on the left, then the green shield on the right, last the small sub-labels.
art: Flat cartoon with thick outlines and soft gradients on the shield. The right car's tank-tread wheels and the glassy shield give a slightly odd mix of styles, but outlines are consistent and the white background is clean, so the scene holds at phone size.
strength: The split-screen with fire on one side and a shield on the other makes the contrast readable without reading any text.
weakness: The two sub-labels are too thin to read at 160x90, so the poor trap versus rich hack naming is lost on small screens.
bottleneck: Sub-labels carry the explanation of each side but sit at the smallest type size in the layout.
action: Hypothesis: enlarge the two sub-labels to roughly the headline's stroke weight and drop the loose bills and bolts to see whether the split reads faster on mobile.
counterexample: Seq 21 uses the same two-label split but gives each half a number (working at 70 versus retired at 55), which adds a specific fact that Seq 1 lacks.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: Two dried clove buds with textured brown heads and cylindrical bodies sit at the left, soft-glowing at their edges. A thick red arrow with a white outline runs from them to the right, aiming at the open mouth of a side-profile anatomical face drawn with exposed red muscle fibres and white teeth. The background is a blurred blue-grey indoor setting.
mechanism: An ingredient-to-body arrow that implies an effect on the mouth or face without naming any result, leaving the outcome for the title and the click.
composition: Cloves fill the left third and the muscle face fills the right half, with the arrow bridging them on a roughly horizontal line at mid-height. The face is cropped at the top and right edge so its mouth is the visual end-point. Scale is large for both subjects and the blurred background keeps the pair separate.
typography: No on-image words, so nothing depends on reading at 160x90. All of the title's story, including the woman, the daily habit and the speed, sits only in the title.
colors: Dark red-brown cloves and saturated red-orange muscle tissue dominate against a cool grey-blue backdrop. The red arrow echoes the muscle colour, so the whole frame leans warm-on-cool with the face and arrow carrying the highest saturation.
psychology: The anatomical face has an open mouth and exposed muscle, which gives a body-focused, clinical impression rather than a visible person's mood. The arrow adds a cause-and-effect cue; no expression, gaze or authority figure is present.
partnership: The title tells a story about a woman, two cloves each day and a fast result, while the thumbnail shows only cloves leading to a mouth and face. The unanswered question is what happens, but the picture hints at a mouth or facial effect and leaves out the woman.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: red arrow and muscle face first, then the two cloves on the left, then the open mouth and teeth as the arrow's target.
art: Glossy rendered look with a soft light halo around the cloves and a hard white outline on the arrow, so the cloves and the face appear cut out and placed on the blurred background. The anatomical face shows plausible muscle striations and the mouth is clear at 160x90.
strength: Clove-arrow-mouth is readable in one glance and the red arrow gives a clear direction.
weakness: The anatomical muscle face is visually intense but gives no concrete outcome, so the viewer cannot tell what the cloves change.
bottleneck: With no words the thumbnail depends on the title for the whole claim and the anatomy image may suggest a symptom the video never shows.
action: Hypothesis: add a short specific noun such as one word naming the body area in question beside the face to test whether a concrete target lifts the story clarity.
counterexample: Seq 22 pairs a similar internal-anatomy graphic with an explicit headline so the claim is stated outright, unlike Seq 2.
medical_notes: The title implies a fast result from a daily spice and the muscle-face image points at the mouth without naming any outcome, so context is needed.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A cartoon man at the left holds both hands to his cheeks with an open mouth and eyes glancing up and to the right. A thick black curved arrow rises from the lower middle toward a large heap of green banded bills at the right edge with loose notes flying. Six white circular labels, $50K, $100K, $250K, $500K, $1M and $2M, sit on stacks of increasing height, and the $500K label has a hand-drawn red ring.
mechanism: An escalating ladder of six labelled money stacks leading to a heap, with a red-ringed milestone that invites the viewer to ask why $500K is flagged.
composition: Subject left, headline centre-top, money pile right: the arrow sweeps from the stack row to the pile, giving a rising diagonal. The stacks form a stair-step along the bottom that supports the idea of levels. The right third is crowded with bills while the left is clean.
typography: Nine words: two stacked bold black lines of headline in the top centre and six small price labels in white circles. The headline reads easily at 160x90 but the six dollar labels shrink to dots, so the ladder numbers are not legible. The title's six levels are visually echoed by six labels without the title's compounding idea.
colors: Black headline and arrow on white, grey shirt on the man and saturated green bills for the money. The single red circle around $500K is the only red accent and so the clearest marker of a milestone.
psychology: Wide eyes, open mouth and hands pressed to the cheeks give an astonished look, matched by the growth arrow. The cues point to surprise and wealth escalation rather than fear.
partnership: The title promises six wealth levels and compounding, and the thumbnail shows six labelled stacks, so it makes the count visible while adding exact dollar steps. The red ring raises an unanswered question about what happens at $500K.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: headline IT GETS CRAZY first, then the arrow's path to the big pile, then the shocked man, last the small dollar labels along the bottom.
art: Clean flat cartoon with thick outline and flat fills; the money pile is dense and detailed but stays on a white background. Stack heights are consistent with the labels, and the circles are a coherent device.
strength: The six rising stacks give a concrete visual ladder that matches the title's count of six levels.
weakness: The six dollar labels are tiny and become unreadable at 160x90, so the ladder reads as generic money piles.
bottleneck: Most of the specific information is in small circular labels while the loud headline carries no number.
action: Hypothesis: keep only three labels at larger size, including the red-ringed $500K, to test whether fewer legible numbers beat six unreadable ones on phones.
counterexample: Seq 20 reduces the numbers to one large figure in the headline, which stays legible at phone size where Seq 3 loses its labels.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A smiling cartoon man with a large rounded head and small round eyes stands at the left in a navy polo with a small ID badge and holds a red toolbox with a grey lid. At the lower centre sit several stacks of green coins with a single dollar-sign coin leaning in front. A thick black curved arrow runs from the headline down to the coins.
mechanism: A tradesman-style character beside a pile of cash with a flat headline that sets a degree-free income outcome, a concrete specific the title also implies.
composition: Character on the left third, headline stack on the upper right, coin piles bottom centre, and a descending arrow tying the text to the coins. The balance is clear and left-to-right, with generous white space between elements.
typography: Two words plus a dollar figure in very thick black condensed capitals on two lines, taking around two fifths of the frame. It is fully legible at 160x90. The number $100K is the information the title does not state, since the title says twelve jobs and no pay figure.
colors: Black text and outlines on white, navy and denim on the man, bright flat green on the coins, and a single red toolbox as a small accent. The coin green is the only strong colour so it carries the money association.
psychology: The man has a closed-mouth smile and relaxed shoulders, which reads as friendly and approachable. The cues suggest an accessible, low-risk message with no urgency or warning.
partnership: The title lists twelve jobs and building wealth, while the thumbnail commits to a single pay figure and the degree angle. It leaves open which jobs, so curiosity remains, but the 12 count is missing.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: huge headline first, then the dollar figure, then the arrow to the coins, then the smiling worker on the left.
art: Simple flat cartoon with outlines of consistent weight, an ID card detail and a toolbox that add a slight job cue. No lighting realism; the coin stacks overlap cleanly. Reads easily on mobile.
strength: Large high-contrast text with the $100K figure makes the claim instantly legible.
weakness: A generic smiling cartoon with a toolbox says tradesperson but does not point to any specific job.
bottleneck: The visual identity of the jobs is vague, so the thumbnail does not suggest the twelve-item list.
action: Hypothesis: add a small row of three distinct job tools or uniforms beside the man to test whether showing variety hints at the list format.
counterexample: Seq 6 uses a similar left-character-plus-headline layout but adds a downward chart arrow, so the visual itself carries a story rather than only a prop.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: Left to right: a brown bear head with a closed mouth and flat gaze, an orange-and-black striped tiger face with wide round eyes, a cassowary with a blue neck and a tall brown casque, and at the right a black-outlined stick figure with a flat-line mouth, one hand on its head and the other held out palm up. The headline is in yellow letters with a dark outline.
mechanism: Three wild animals turned toward the viewer next to a puzzled stick figure turns the headline question into a visual one without saying what is known.
composition: Animals are clustered in the lower left half and cropped by the frame, with the stick figure on the right and the headline centred above. The horizontal row of faces forms a line at the bottom and the empty white band above the animals gives the headline room.
typography: Three words on two lines in thick yellow outlined capitals, about a third of the frame height. Legible at 160x90. The pronoun THEY depends on the animals and the title for context, and the words help and wild animals appear only in the title.
colors: Yellow headline on white, warm brown and orange animals, and a bright blue cassowary neck as the sharpest cool accent. The stick figure is black-and-white so it recedes while the animals dominate.
psychology: The tiger and cassowary show wide round eyes while the bear has a closed flat mouth, and the stick figure has a flat-line mouth with a hand on its head. These cartoon cues give a puzzled, questioning pose rather than urgency.
partnership: The title adds the specific idea of help and wild animals, while the thumbnail offers only an ambiguous pronoun that the animal faces resolve. The unanswered question is what the animals know, which is a strong curiosity gap with no spoiler.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow DO THEY KNOW first, then the tiger's wide-eyed face, then the cassowary, then the stick figure's gesture on the right.
art: Flat doodle style with consistent outline weight on both the animals and stick figure. The cropped animals are slightly crowded, but a clean white background keeps the thumbnail simple and legible at phone size.
strength: Animal faces plus a puzzled stick figure make a clear question in seconds.
weakness: The animals are not shown in any act of helping, so the title's help element is not visualised.
bottleneck: The pronoun THEY has no explicit referent in the text, so the image must do all of that work.
action: Hypothesis: add a small hand or rescue object entering from the right toward one animal to test whether showing help sharpens what is being asked.
counterexample: Seq 10 has no stick-figure reaction at all and relies on a headline alone, leaving the viewer without a human proxy.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A cartoon man with an egg-shaped head, sweat drops on the forehead, wide eyes and an open slack mouth holds both palms up in front of his white polo. At the right a thick red zigzag arrow descends across a faint grid over four gold coin stacks that shrink in height from left to right. A black curved arrow points from the headline toward the chart.
mechanism: A visible decline chart of shrinking coin stacks and a worried figure carry a negative-trend story that the headline states in four words.
composition: Man on the left third, headline upper right, and a descending red arrow cutting diagonally through the chart on the right half. The red arrow's downward diagonal pulls the eye to the bottom-right corner, and white space around the headline keeps it clean.
typography: Three words on two lines in heavy black condensed capitals filling the upper right. High contrast and fully readable at 160x90. The title names investing, while the thumbnail text omits it and relies on the coin stacks to convey the money topic.
colors: Black headline on white, a saturated red decline arrow and gold coin stacks, with a blue-denim and white outfit. Red is used for the falling line and signals loss, making it the clearest accent.
psychology: Sweat drops, wide round eyes, open mouth and raised palms read as alarm or a stop gesture. Together with the red downward line they cue worry and a negative trend.
partnership: The title promises the biggest problem with investing and the thumbnail shows a decline without naming the problem. Both emphasise negativity, with the unresolved question being what is getting worse and why.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: black headline first, then the red falling arrow, then the sweating man's face, then the dwindling coin stacks.
art: Flat cartoon with consistent outline and simple gradients on the coins. The red arrow and the grid read as a stylised chart; elements do not overlap confusingly, so it holds up on mobile.
strength: A red falling arrow over shrinking coins turns an abstract complaint into an instantly legible picture.
weakness: The problem itself is never named, so the thumbnail could fit any market-decline video.
bottleneck: Generic decline visuals lack a specific object or number that would make this video distinct from other bearish ones.
action: Hypothesis: replace one coin stack with a labelled object or a percentage figure to test whether one concrete detail beats the generic decline motif.
counterexample: Seq 3 shows the same cartoon style with an upward arrow and escalating stacks, making the opposite trend visible.
expression_label: wide eyes, open mouth, raised palms, sweat drops
hero_object: falling red arrow over coin stacks
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A large cartoon man with a half-lidded look and a slight smile at the left holds a stack of green bills banded with a $100K label. At the lower right a much smaller cartoon man in a dark suit and tie with a small chest badge stands with hands raised and wide eyes. A thick black curved arrow connects the headline to the small man. The native file is only 360 by 202 pixels.
mechanism: Size contrast between the cash-holding figure and a flinching suited figure turns the headline into a scene, with the exact amount from the title shown on the bills.
composition: Large man on the left third, headline in the top right, and the small suited man in the lower right pointed to by the arrow. The scale difference places the cash holder as dominant and the small man as the payoff. Space is open and the layout is simple.
typography: Three headline words in heavy black capitals on two lines plus a small $100K on the bill band, so four items in all. The headline survives at 160x90 but the $100K label and the small man's badge become unreadable specks. The title names banks and the exact amount, while the headline uses a pronoun for banks.
colors: Black text on white, a muted cream and blue-grey for the large man and a dark suit for the small one, with green bills as the only saturated accent. The low overall saturation makes the cash stack the clearest colour object.
psychology: The small man has wide eyes, raised hands and a leaning pose that reads as flinching. The big figure's half-closed eyes and slight smile suggest relaxed confidence, forming a power-reversal cue.
partnership: The title spells out banks and $100,000, and the thumbnail shows the same amount while the small suited figure stands for the bank. The picture adds the intimidation scene but the text uses THEY, so the title does the identifying work.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: bold headline first, then the arrow, then the tiny frightened suited man, then the stack of $100K bills in the big man's hand.
art: Flat cartoon at low resolution; outlines look slightly soft because the file is small, but the shapes are clear. The scale mismatch is a deliberate device rather than an artefact.
strength: Big-versus-tiny scale contrast delivers the power-reversal idea at once.
weakness: The $100K label and the banker's badge are too small to read at phone size, so the bank link relies on the title.
bottleneck: The small suited man carries the key referent but occupies the smallest area of the frame.
action: Hypothesis: enlarge the small suited man and add a one-word badge such as BANK to test whether naming the referent reduces reliance on the title.
counterexample: Seq 20 also shows a relaxed cash-linked figure but pairs it with a single large headline figure that survives phone size better.
expression_label: relaxed half-lidded smile vs wide-eyed flinch
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: THE REAL REASON / COFFEE / CLOGS YOUR / ARTERIES!
scene: At the right an older man with a shaved head and grey beard looks straight out with raised brows and a closed mouth. He wears teal scrubs, a white coat and a stethoscope, holds a glass French press of dark coffee in one hand and points at his chest with the other. A small red curved arrow runs from the word COFFEE toward the press. Part of a name on the coat, starting Dr. M, is cut off at the right edge.
mechanism: A doctor-styled figure holding the coffee press under a block of alarm text frames coffee as a hidden danger, with the headline naming the artery claim directly.
composition: Text column fills the left half on a purple panel and the man fills the right half on a red-orange backdrop. The French press sits at the centre seam between them and the red arrow links word to object. A purple banner across the top holds the lead-in.
typography: Seven words in four rows: a smaller white lead-in in a purple bar, then COFFEE in yellow-orange, CLOGS YOUR in white and ARTERIES! in yellow, all with heavy outlines. All rows remain legible at 160x90. The title's age 60 and not caffeine details are absent from the thumbnail, which adds the arteries claim.
colors: Purple, red-orange and yellow dominate with white text and teal scrubs as the cool break. Red and the yellow headline signal urgency and warning, and the high saturation separates the man from the background.
psychology: Raised brows, a closed straight mouth and direct frontal gaze with a stethoscope and white coat give a serious authority-and-concern look. The pointing hand and the red backdrop add a warning cue.
partnership: The title says coffee is dangerous after 60 for a reason other than caffeine, while the thumbnail escalates to a specific arteries claim and drops the age and the not-caffeine twist. The real reason is promised but not named, leaving a gap.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow COFFEE first, then ARTERIES!, then the man's face and gaze on the right, then the French press at the seam.
art: Composited look: the man and French press are sharply cut against a flat red-orange panel and a purple-black text panel, with a bright rim edge on the left of the man. The coat's name text is partly cropped and only partly readable.
strength: Strong headline hierarchy and a doctor-styled figure give a clear, loud claim even at small size.
weakness: The artery claim is stated as flat fact and the partly cropped name on the coat gives an unclear credential.
bottleneck: A severe disease claim is delivered through alarm styling without any qualifier on the image.
action: Hypothesis: soften the headline to a question form such as does coffee clog arteries and test it against the current declarative wording.
counterexample: Seq 9 shows a visibly calm doctor-styled woman with a plain question and no alarm colours, the opposite register.
expression_label: raised brows, closed mouth, direct gaze
medical_notes: The headline states an artery-clogging claim as fact beside a doctor-styled figure whose coat name is partly cropped, so the packaging overstates risk and credential clarity.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: DOES GETTING A / MEMORY LOSS / EVALUATION / MATTER? / Helping Older Parents with Memory Loss [logo: two outlined figures walking, one with a cane]
scene: A woman with dark curly hair, small gold drop earrings and a closed-mouth smile looks at the camera from a rounded-corner photo on the right. She wears a white coat over a maroon blouse with a beaded necklace and a blue stethoscope around the neck, in front of a blurred city-street backdrop. A thin-line logo of two walking figures, one using a cane, sits bottom left beside a tagline.
mechanism: A calm clinician portrait next to a four-line question headline frames a memory-evaluation question as a straightforward explainer, not an alarm.
composition: Text block occupies the left half and the rounded portrait fills the right, creating a clean two-column split. The headline's four stacked lines and the bottom-left logo create a left-aligned reading path, while the portrait sits slightly right of centre with the face in the upper-right third.
typography: Seven headline words in four lines of heavy sans capitals, the middle two lines in white and the others in black, plus a six-word smaller tagline beside the logo. The headline is large and readable at 160x90, while the tagline shrinks to thin marks. It rephrases the title as a question and adds the idea of whether it matters.
colors: A flat mint-teal background with black and white headline and a warm skin-tone portrait with a maroon accent. The palette is calm and low in contrast between teal and white, so MEMORY LOSS in white sits slightly weaker than the black lines.
psychology: The woman's gentle closed-mouth smile and direct gaze with a stethoscope and white coat give a visible friendly-clinician look. The cues are reassurance and professional approachability, with no fear or urgency elements.
partnership: The title tells viewers to get a parent's memory evaluated, and the thumbnail asks whether it matters, posing the title as a question and adding the framing of a doubt. The unanswered question is clear but low-stakes, and nothing is shown that would reveal the answer.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: black headline lines first, then the portrait's face, then the white MEMORY LOSS words, last the bottom-left logo and tagline.
art: Straight portrait photograph cropped into a rounded rectangle on a flat template background; lighting on the face is even and natural-looking with a shallow depth blur behind. No cutout artefacts are visible, and the template look is plain but coherent.
strength: A clear question headline beside a friendly clinician portrait is easy to parse and feels trustworthy.
weakness: The template layout has no visual tension or concrete object, so it shows little to make this video distinct from other talking-head explainers.
bottleneck: With a flat colour field and a neutral smile there is no visible stake to create urgency about the evaluation.
action: Hypothesis: replace the plain smile with a concerned-but-calm expression and add one concrete prop, such as a clipboard or a clock, to test whether a visible stake lifts the hook.
counterexample: Seq 8 puts a doctor-styled figure under loud yellow and red alarm text, the opposite register of this calm mint template.
medical_notes: A neutral question headline with a clinician-styled portrait makes no cure, diagnosis or fear claim, though no credential name is printed.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: Two sheep heads stand side by side in front of a hand-drawn farm with a red barn, a windmill, a wooden fence, a tree and two small sheep in the field. The white sheep on the left has pink ears and a single red eye placed in the centre of its face. The black sheep on the right has two eyes, one blue and one orange. Both have patchy tan, grey and black wool on their bodies.
mechanism: Two sheep with unusual eyes under a headline about a one-in-a-billion rarity make the rarity itself the picture, with the viewer left to ask which trait it means.
composition: The two heads sit side by side in the lower two thirds and fill the width, while the headline spans the top. The white and black heads create a strong light-dark pair with the eyes as the small focal points. The farm background is softly muted behind them.
typography: Four words in rounded yellow letters with a black outline across the top in a single line. They remain readable at 160x90. The title speaks of the rarest animal traits and the thumbnail adds the one-in-a-billion odds without naming the trait.
colors: Pale blue sky, green fields and a red barn behind with a white sheep and a black sheep in the foreground. The red barn and the coloured eyes are the small saturated accents, while yellow text is the brightest element.
psychology: Both sheep face the viewer with neutral closed mouths and steady gaze, which creates a staring, uncanny feel. The mismatched eye colours and the single centred eye give an unusual-feature cue.
partnership: The title promises a list of rare traits, and the thumbnail focuses on a single extreme odds claim with two visible oddities. The question of which one is the one in a billion stays open, and the pairing hints at at least two traits.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow headline first, then the white sheep's single red eye, then the black sheep's blue and orange eyes, then the barn background.
art: Hand-drawn digital illustration with textured wool and an even outline weight. The white sheep's face has one eye in the centre and its body has a pale limb shape at the lower left, which are consistent with the intended oddity but anatomically strange. The background is detailed yet softened.
strength: Two contrasting heads with unusual eyes make the rarity visible and memorable.
weakness: The eyes are small details and the single-eye trait is hard to see at 160x90, so the oddity is partly lost on phones.
bottleneck: The rarity is carried by tiny eye details while the large wool and farm areas carry no information.
action: Hypothesis: zoom the frame to the two faces and enlarge the eyes so that the unusual traits are visible at 160x90.
counterexample: Seq 13 has larger readable action details like a mammoth and spear that stay recognisable at phone size, unlike the small eye details here.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: BANANA + BP? / [device display: SYS 158, DIA 92, PULSE 78]
scene: At the right a bearded man with dark hair and rectangular glasses wears blue scrubs with a stethoscope draped over his neck, holds a yellow banana in one hand and extends the other palm up with raised brows and slightly open mouth. At the left sits a white upper-arm blood-pressure monitor with its cuff, showing 158, 92 and 78 on the screen. The background is a dark blurred kitchen.
mechanism: A banana in the clinician's hand next to a blood pressure monitor showing a high reading turns the headline pair into a literal object pairing with a question mark.
composition: Headline spans the top left and the man fills the right third, with the monitor bottom left and the banana at the centre of the frame forming a triangle between them. The banana is the central link between the device and the man's gesture, and the dark background isolates all three.
typography: Two overlay words in big condensed capitals with a plus sign, BANANA in white and BP? in red, filling the top two thirds of the width. They are fully legible at 160x90. The display digits are part of the photographed device rather than overlay text. The thumbnail drops the title's after-60 and potassium details.
colors: Dark charcoal and near-black background with a yellow banana and blue scrubs as the saturated points, plus white headline and red BP. The red BP echoes the high reading, and the yellow banana is the strongest colour object.
psychology: The man's raised eyebrows, slightly open mouth, direct gaze and open palm look like explaining or questioning, backed by a stethoscope and scrubs. The 158 over 92 display adds a visible health-concern cue.
partnership: The title adds age 60 and potassium, while the thumbnail pairs banana and BP in a short question. The monitor reading prompts the question of whether bananas help or hurt, and no answer is revealed.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: white BANANA first, then red BP?, then the yellow banana, then the man's gesturing face, last the monitor numbers.
art: Photographic with controlled studio-style lighting and consistent shadows across the man, banana and monitor. The three subjects look to share the same scene, and the hand holding the banana is anatomically coherent. The dark background keeps all items clear at 160x90.
strength: Banana, monitor and clinician in one frame pose the title's relationship as a single concrete question.
weakness: The thumbnail drops the age 60 and potassium angle that the title uses to define the audience.
bottleneck: Nothing signals who the video is for, so the target viewer must be taken from the title.
action: Hypothesis: add a small 60+ tag beside BP to test whether naming the audience increases fit without crowding the headline.
counterexample: Seq 12 packs five lines of text around a cartoon figure, while this thumbnail uses two words and real objects.
medical_notes: The banana beside a high-reading monitor can imply a remedy for blood pressure, but the question form leaves the claim open.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: HOW OFTEN / SHOULD SENIORS / SHOWER? / ONES OR TWICE / A WEEK
scene: A shirtless cartoon older man with short grey hair and a slight smile, wearing teal shorts, rubs his arm with a yellow sponge while water from a wall-mounted shower head sprays at him, with water drops flying from the arm. A small dark panel with three droplet icons and a chrome mixer sit beside the shower on the right. The background is solid black.
mechanism: A frequency question with the answer printed beneath it, shown with a washing older man, so the thumbnail already gives the headline's reply.
composition: Five lines of text stack down the left two thirds and the man with the shower fills the right third. The red bar under SHOWER? is the strongest block and the text column leads the eye down to A WEEK. The man stands upright in a narrow strip so the stacking is left-heavy.
typography: Ten words in five rows with three styles: yellow capitals for the first two rows, white on a red rectangle for SHOWER?, and white capitals below. The sizes shrink down the column and the last two rows are thinner at 160x90 but still readable. The text uses shower where the title says bath and misspells once as ONES, and it restates the question while adding a frequency answer.
colors: Black background with yellow, white and a saturated red bar for the headline, with a tan skin tone and bright teal shorts for the figure. The red bar acts as a high-alert emphasis block around SHOWER?, and the teal shorts are the cool accent.
psychology: The man has a calm, slight closed-mouth smile and an everyday scrubbing pose, so the visible tone is plain and routine. Urgency comes from the red block and bold text rather than from his expression.
partnership: The title says bath and promises seven shocking facts, while the thumbnail says shower and states the answer ones or twice a week. The overlay therefore spends the main curiosity and does not echo the shocking angle.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow HOW OFTEN first, then the red SHOWER? bar, then the white answer lines, then the man at the shower on the right.
art: Digital cartoon with smooth fills and consistent outlines on a black background. The shower, sponge and water are coherent and the man's anatomy reads correctly, but the five-line text block is dense for a small screen.
strength: High-contrast yellow and red text on black makes the first two lines pop clearly.
weakness: The bottom two lines are the smallest and carry the answer, while the typo ONES lowers polish.
bottleneck: Ten words in five rows crowd the frame and the answer is spoken in the weakest text size.
action: Hypothesis: cut the text to HOW OFTEN SHOWER? with the red bar and test whether withholding the frequency answer improves curiosity.
counterexample: Seq 11 gives only two big words and lets objects carry the idea, so it avoids this thumbnail's dense text column.
medical_notes: The thumbnail states a hygiene frequency for seniors and says shower while the title says bath, so the packaging needs context.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A large close-up stick-style figure with shaggy brown hair, round eyes glancing up to the right, a raised brow and a flat mouth holds a stone-tipped spear in a fur tunic at the lower left. Behind it a woolly mammoth with curved tusks has a spear stuck in its side, surrounded by four small spear-carrying figures on a brown plain with snowy mountains and blue sky.
mechanism: A reaction-faced stick figure in front of a speared mammoth and four tiny hunters turns the question into a scene with scale contrast.
composition: The big figure occupies the lower left and the mammoth sits right of centre, with a diagonal from the spear tip to the mammoth's trunk. The small hunters ring the mammoth at lower scale, and the headline spans the whole top edge. The horizon is high.
typography: Three words in one line of yellow capitals with a black outline across the top, easily legible at 160x90. The phrase names mammoths, which the title only calls giant animals, and drops the how-question.
colors: A pale blue sky, grey-blue mountains and brown-tan plain with a yellow headline as the brightest element. Mammoth brown blends with the ground, so the mammoth separates mainly by size and outline.
psychology: The foreground figure has raised eyebrows, side-glancing eyes and a flat mouth, which give a sceptical, puzzled look. The small hunters with spears show effort, and nothing in the frame suggests fear.
partnership: The title asks how ancient humans hunted giant animals and the thumbnail specialises that to mammoths with a doubtful question. The speared mammoth and tiny hunters offer a partial answer, so the scene hints at the method.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow headline first, then the big face and its side glance, then the mammoth with the spear in it, then the small hunters.
art: Mixed styles: a simple stick-figure foreground against a more detailed furry mammoth and shaded mountains. Outline and fill weights are consistent enough for the mix to read as one scene, and the mammoth remains recognisable at phone size.
strength: The scale contrast between the giant mammoth and tiny hunters directly shows the title's giant animals.
weakness: The large foreground face and the mammoth compete for attention, and the question mark leaves the tone unclear.
bottleneck: Two focal areas of similar weight split attention and delay the read of the hunting story.
action: Hypothesis: shrink the foreground figure by a third and move it to the corner so the mammoth and hunters become the single focal point.
counterexample: Seq 15 uses one large face and a minimal background, giving a single focal point where Seq 13 has two.
expression_label: raised brow, side glance, flat mouth
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A red circle at bottom left holds a small black dinosaur silhouette hanging in a sling and the words what if?
mechanism: A floating stick figure with two onlookers shows the title's premise as a plain picture, and the channel badge adds a recognisable brand mark instead of a headline.
composition: Three figures are spread across the width at different heights, with the floating one at the top centre. The ground line anchors the lower third and the red badge sits at the bottom left corner. White space is generous and the figures form a loose triangle.
typography: Only the badge text what if? in white lowercase on the red circle, two words and small. It is legible at 160x90 as a mark but carries no information about the one-foot-per-second claim. The title's number and unit appear nowhere in the image.
colors: Black line art on pure white with a single red-and-black circular badge, giving a stark two-colour palette. The red badge is the only colour accent and so is the brightest spot in an otherwise neutral frame.
psychology: The heads are blank circles with no drawn expressions, so emotion comes from posture: an exclamation mark beside the left figure, a raised arm and an outstretched reaching arm. These cues suggest surprise at the floating figure.
partnership: The title states a precise rate of one foot per second and the thumbnail shows only the moment of lift-off. The answer to what happens next is not hinted, but the specific figure is missing from the image.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the floating central figure first, then the left figure with the exclamation mark, then the reaching figure on the right, then the red badge at the corner.
art: Hand-drawn line art with uneven stroke weight, characteristic of a sketch style; no digital artefacts are visible. The figures are minimal and coherent, and the large white space gives a clean look at phone size.
strength: A clean sketch with a floating figure is instantly understandable and stands out against busier thumbnails.
weakness: No numbers or words describe the rate, so the one-foot-per-second hook from the title is not visible.
bottleneck: The only text is a small channel badge, so the specific premise has to come entirely from the title.
action: Hypothesis: add a small 1 ft/s label beside the lower arcs to test whether showing the specific rate improves title and thumbnail fit.
counterexample: Seq 3 puts six dollar figures into its image and uses numbers as the hook, the opposite of this numberless frame.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A shaggy-haired cartoon man with white face, wide eyes with raised worried brows and a slightly open slanted mouth presses a grey pointed stone against his left cheek (viewer's left). A long curly brown beard hangs from the right side of his chin. The background is a flat blue sky above a green field with a blue river running in from the right.
mechanism: The stone pressed to a half-bearded cheek makes the title's rock-shaving idea visible in one image, with the wary face adding doubt.
composition: The face is centred and takes up most of the height, with the headline spanning the top and the river curving in at the lower right. The diagonal of the river pulls the eye towards the beard. The background has only three flat colour zones, so the face is clear.
typography: Three words in a single line of thick yellow capitals with black outline, large and readable at 160x90. The phrase repeats the title's core and drops how and ancient humans, so it adds nothing beyond the picture.
colors: Saturated cyan-blue sky and bright green grass with a brown beard and hair and yellow text. The strong blue and green fill the background, so the brown hair and beard are the dark focal mass.
psychology: Raised, inward-slanted brows, wide eyes and a slightly open flat mouth give a visible nervous or hesitant expression as the stone touches the face. The beard on one side only suggests a mid-shave state.
partnership: The title asks how ancient humans did it, and the thumbnail repeats the shaving-with-rocks phrase while showing the stone and beard. The visible half-shave is a mild reveal, but how it works stays unanswered.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow headline first, then the worried face and stone on the cheek, then the long beard on the right, last the river.
art: Flat cartoon with thick black outlines and uniform fills; the beard has fine scribbled curls that add texture. The grey stone and hand overlap cleanly and the anatomy reads simply.
strength: One large expressive face with a stone on the cheek makes the premise immediate.
weakness: The headline repeats the title almost word for word, so it contributes no extra curiosity.
bottleneck: The ancient-humans context is carried only by the shaggy hair and the title.
action: Hypothesis: replace the headline with a short reaction line such as DID IT WORK? to test whether adding a new question beats repeating the title.
counterexample: Seq 13 spreads the idea across a mammoth and hunters instead of one face, showing a richer scene.
expression_label: raised worried brows, wide eyes, slanted mouth
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: In a pale clinical room with shelves, a plant, a wall anatomy poster and an exam table at the right, a smooth featureless white head tops a figure in a black cardigan, white shirt, grey trousers and black shoes. The figure wears white gloves and leans on a cane in the hand at the viewer's left. A glowing red heart with a red ECG line is placed on the chest, and red numerals 60 with a comma sit at the shoes. A small white four-point star mark appears at the bottom right.
mechanism: A faceless older-styled figure with a glowing heart on the chest and an age number frames a heart-risk message for people in their sixties, with the calf pain from the title not shown.
composition: Vertical Shorts frame with the figure centred and spanning roughly four-fifths of the height (head near the top, feet near the bottom), the heart at upper chest as the focal point and 60 at the bottom as a second anchor. The desaturated room and the figure's grey clothes make the red heart the one colour point. Symmetry is strong.
typography: A single numeral and comma in thick red with a dark outline near the shoes, one word in all. It is tiny relative to the frame and is nearly lost at 160x90. The title carries the calf pain, heart disease question and hashtags that are absent from the image.
colors: Almost monochrome greys, white and black with the red heart glow and the red 60 as the only saturated accents. The red against grey makes the heart stand out, and the glow reads as a danger cue.
psychology: The head has no visible face, so there is no expression or gaze. The cane, grey clothes and glowing heart create a vulnerability cue through posture and objects, and the red glow adds an alarm cue.
partnership: The title asks whether calf pain is actually heart disease, while the thumbnail shows only a heart on the chest and the number 60 and does not depict a calf. The age number adds audience information, but the calf-to-heart link is not visualised.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the glowing red heart first, then the blank white head, then the cane and the legs down to the red 60 at the bottom.
art: Smooth, mannequin-like figure with a glossy blank head and white hands, set in a clean room with soft lighting; the red heart is a glowing overlay. The 60 text sits on top of the shoes and the star mark is wordless. The room is plain and the subject is clear.
strength: A single red heart on a grey figure is a strong colour contrast and an easy focal point.
weakness: The 60 numeral and ECG line are very small, and the calf-pain premise from the title is not shown anywhere.
bottleneck: The only text is a tiny fragment at the bottom while the main claim sits in the title and hashtags.
action: Hypothesis: place a red highlight on one calf of the figure with a short LEG PAIN? label to test whether linking the two body parts improves title fit.
counterexample: Seq 11 shows a real clinician and a banana with a large headline, making the health question concrete instead of symbolic.
medical_notes: The title links calf pain to heart disease and the image shows a glowing chest heart instead of a leg, so the symptom imagery needs context.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: Against a teal wall and tan floor, a stick-limbed figure in a pink-red hooded suit with a black circle-masked face stands at the right and holds a long dark-handled tool with a flat paddle end resting on the floor. At the lower left a white-headed stick figure in a green top marked with the number 2 lies motionless on its side on the floor.
mechanism: Two role costumes from a known game, one standing with a tool and one lying down, show a rank contrast with a very short headline naming the franchise.
composition: The masked figure towers on the right with a diagonal tool line running down to the left, where the small lying figure sits low. The headline fills the upper left. The diagonal and the size contrast give a clear top-down order between standing and lying figures.
typography: Three words in two rows: SQUID GAMES in pink outlined capitals and RANKS in white outlined capitals below, taking the upper-left half. Both rows are legible at 160x90. The text names the franchise and the idea of ranks, while the title adds the viewer's own life.
colors: Muted teal wall with beige floor, a saturated pink-red suit and a deep green tracksuit as the colour accents. The pink-red headline matches the guard's suit, tying text to character, and the white RANKS gives a second tone.
psychology: The masked guard has no visible face, only a circle on black, and the lying figure has a blank white head. Meaning comes from posture and size: one figure standing over the other with a tool.
partnership: The title says your life as every rank, and the thumbnail shows two characters from the series and one rank word, so it pictures only two ranks. The you angle and the every part of the title are not shown.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: pink SQUID GAMES first, then the masked guard's black face, then the tool pointing down, then the lying numbered figure.
art: Flat vector with consistent outline weight between the stick limbs and the filled costumes. The stylised costumes and the simple room are coherent, and the contrast between colour fields keeps it clear on mobile.
strength: Recognisable franchise costumes and a simple standing-versus-lying pose read quickly.
weakness: Only two roles appear, and the lying figure is the smallest and lowest element, so the every-rank scope is not suggested.
bottleneck: The viewer's own life, which is the title's hook, has no visual stand-in in the frame.
action: Hypothesis: add a third small figure in a different costume at the far left to test whether showing more than two ranks signals the every-rank scope.
counterexample: Seq 21 labels each side with a number and role, so its contrast is spelled out, while this one leaves the ranks unlabelled.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A cartoon young man with black spiky hair, half-lidded eyes and a closed-mouth smile leans on the bonnet of a rusty brown sedan. He wears a black jacket over a white tee, holds a paper coffee cup in one hand and keeps the other in his pocket. A phone on the bonnet shows a green screen with a figure whose digits are smudged. Behind him in a car park, three men in dark suits stand near a black SUV, a white sedan and a black sedan: one holds up a phone, one laughs with a raised hand, one looks down at a phone.
mechanism: A casual figure with a rusty car and a large balance on a phone is set against suited men and luxury cars, so the quiet-millionaire idea is told by contrast rather than words.
composition: The character stands centred and fills most of the height, with the old car at the lower left and the suited men and luxury cars in the upper right background. The phone on the bonnet sits low as a small secondary point. A wide, calm horizon and soft sky leave no text zone.
typography: No on-image text at all, so the whole concept depends on the title and the small phone screen, whose digits are blurred. At 160x90 nothing readable survives except the face and shapes.
colors: Desaturated blue-grey sky and buildings, brown-orange rust on the car, black clothes and a small bright green phone screen. The only saturated spot is the phone, which is also the least legible element.
psychology: The man's half-closed eyes and slight smile with a hand in the pocket give a relaxed, unbothered look. The suited men's smiling, selfie and phone poses add a contrast of status through gestures.
partnership: The title promises a day in a quiet millionaire's life, and the thumbnail shows an unassuming man with an old car, which fits quiet. The wealth cue sits only on the tiny phone screen, so the millionaire part is mostly from the title.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the character's face first, then the rusty car, then the group of suited men on the right, last the phone on the bonnet.
art: Clean digital cartoon with soft shading and consistent perspective across the car park. The phone's numerals are garbled rather than crisp, and the background is detailed but kept in muted tones so the character stays central.
strength: The rusty car with a relaxed character against luxury cars tells the quiet-wealth idea without any text.
weakness: The phone balance is too small and its digits smudged, so the millionaire cue is lost at phone size.
bottleneck: Wealth is signalled only by a tiny screen while the largest elements look ordinary.
action: Hypothesis: enlarge the phone screen and render a legible amount such as $2,000,000 to test whether a readable figure strengthens the millionaire cue.
counterexample: Seq 4 states its pay figure in a huge headline, so the money cue stays readable where this thumbnail's does not.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: On a white background a hand-drawn manga-style woman in a tall black headdress with a row of yellow beads and fluffy cream trim has green eyes, a pursed closed mouth and gold tassel earrings. She wears an orange robe patterned with gold leaves, blue sleeves with cloud patterns, long pink-bead necklaces and a fluffy white collar. At the right a thin black arrow curves from the text toward her, and a small circular logo sits at the top left.
mechanism: A regal costumed figure beside a casual handwritten line frames a scheming-empress story, with the arrow connecting the phrase to the character.
composition: The figure fills the left half and is cropped at the top and bottom, with the text on the right and a curved arrow between. The huge empty white space on the right gives the handwriting room, but the figure's vivid costume dominates the balance.
typography: Three words in two lines of thin black handwritten-style letters, with a small circular logo of two words in the corner. The text is readable at 160x90 but light in weight against the heavy costume. The title only says empress, so the seduction angle comes from the thumbnail text.
colors: Pure white background with saturated orange and blue costume, black headdress and gold accents. The orange robe is the strongest mass, and the black thin text is much lighter in visual weight.
psychology: The woman's slight frown and level green-eyed gaze with a lowered head give a stern, composed look. Opulent costume and headdress signal rank and authority.
partnership: The title says your life as an empress, while the thumbnail text states a specific event, seduced an empire, adding a plot hook. The pairing leaves open how and why, and the viewer is not shown as the subject.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the orange robe and face first, then the handwritten Seduced an Empire, then the arrow, then the corner logo.
art: Anime-like digital drawing with fine line work, soft cel shading and detailed patterns on the robe. The fur trim looks painted with a rough brush and the figure is cleanly cut against white. Anatomy and costume are coherent.
strength: A richly detailed costume against a white field draws the eye strongly and signals a historical-royal subject.
weakness: The thin handwritten text has far less visual weight than the costume, so the hook phrase is easy to miss.
bottleneck: Heavy colour on the figure outweighs the light hook line at the right.
action: Hypothesis: set Seduced an Empire in a bold weight and a colour from the robe to test whether a stronger headline increases reading priority.
counterexample: Seq 9 also pairs a calm face with side text but sets the headline in very heavy capitals, so its words carry far more weight than this thin handwriting.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A cartoon man with brown hair, dark sunglasses and a closed mouth in a navy blazer and jeans reclines in a blue folding chair on a bed of green coin discs. Beside him a tent-style flip calendar shows two zigzag lines, and between the chair and the calendar a jagged red crack opens in the coin pile. A thick black curved arrow points from the headline toward the calendar.
mechanism: A relaxed figure on a cash pile next to a cracked ground and a trend sheet pairs a single dollar threshold with a hint of risk, with the headline naming the amount as a rule.
composition: The man sits at the left and the big headline fills the right two thirds, stacking THE, the figure and RULE. The calendar and the red crack form a small cluster at the lower middle, and the arrow loops back toward them from the right. The lower edge of RULE touches the calendar top.
typography: Three words stacked, with the dollar figure far larger than the others in heavy black condensed capitals. It remains legible at 160x90 as one dominant number. The title says everything changes after hitting $250,000 invested and the thumbnail keeps the amount while dropping the change.
colors: Black headline on white with a green coin mat, a navy blazer and blue chair, and red crack lines as the single warm accent. The red crack stands out as an alert mark in an otherwise green-black scheme.
psychology: Sunglasses hide the eyes and the reclined posture with folded hands is relaxed. The red fracture beside him adds a visible risk cue that contrasts with his calm pose.
partnership: The title speaks of everything changing after $250,000, and the thumbnail turns that into a named rule with the same figure. The cracked ground and the chart hint at a shift, but the rule itself is not stated.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the huge $250,000 first, then the arrow, then the red crack and calendar, then the reclining man on the left.
art: Flat cartoon with consistent outlines. The coin discs fill the lower band repetitively and the red crack is a clear device; the calendar overlaps the headline edge slightly, but the headline stays readable.
strength: One enormous dollar figure makes the topic and threshold clear even at 160x90.
weakness: The red crack and the calendar chart are small and ambiguous, so the change the title promises is not obvious.
bottleneck: The visual story of what changes at $250,000 is limited to two small props while the number does all the work.
action: Hypothesis: enlarge the crack and add a before-and-after pair of chair positions to test whether a visible change strengthens the title match.
counterexample: Seq 6 uses a worried face and a falling red arrow, an opposite negative mood to this relaxed pose.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: THE RETIREMENT TRAP / WORKING AT 70 / RETIRED AT 55
scene: A vertical line splits the frame. On the left a smiling cartoon man with glasses in a navy suit strides forward with a raised fist and a brown briefcase. On the right a green-skinned skeleton-like figure with exposed ribs and hollow eyes sits in a rocking chair in a tattered gown, with an IV bag on a stand connected to its arm, facing an old television showing static. A red warning triangle with an exclamation mark sits at the bottom right.
mechanism: An exaggerated two-panel contrast of a busy worker and a decaying retiree, with age labels on each side, gives the death-spiral idea a shocking visual.
composition: Top-centre headline, two age labels under it, and two figures separated by a clean vertical line. The left figure moves toward the right with energy and the right figure is static in the chair, so the panels differ in motion. The warning triangle anchors the lower-right corner.
typography: Nine words: a red heavy headline on one line and two smaller black labels, WORKING AT 70 and RETIRED AT 55, above the panels. The headline stays legible at 160x90, but the two labels thin out. The numbers add the age contrast that the title lacks.
colors: Red headline and warning triangle on white, a navy suit and a sickly green skin tone on the right figure. The red marks danger on the retirement side and the green skin colours it as unwell.
psychology: The left man has a wide open smile and a raised fist, while the right figure has hollow eyes, open mouth and exposed bones, giving a fear and decay cue. The triangle and drip bag add a visible alarm cue.
partnership: The title makes a claim that you die when you stop working, and the thumbnail dramatises it with a skeleton figure and the ages 55 and 70. The thumbnail adds the numbers and the trap framing and goes further by showing death imagery.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: red headline first, then the skeletal figure in the chair, then the smiling worker on the left, then the age labels and the warning triangle.
art: Flat cartoon with thick outlines on both panels. The skeleton figure with exposed ribs, IV tube and television static is coherent in design, and the white background keeps the panels clean.
strength: The sharply different panels with specific ages make a clear, memorable contrast.
weakness: The decay imagery is extreme and the age labels are too thin at phone size.
bottleneck: Specific ages carry the new information in the smallest type on the frame.
action: Hypothesis: enlarge the two age labels to about two thirds of the headline height to test whether the numbers register at 160x90.
counterexample: Seq 1 uses the same split-panel layout without numbers or a warning triangle, so it states less specific information.
expression_label: wide smile vs hollow-eyed open mouth
medical_notes: The finance topic is paired with a skeleton and IV imagery implying that retiring causes death, so the mortality claim needs context.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: JUST 1 CUP / REMOVES / KILOS OF / TOXIC FECES
scene: On a black background a large pink-orange cutaway of the large intestine surrounds a coil of small intestine, with the descending part opened to show a cluster of brown stool lumps. Four lines of text sit to the left, with the last two words in white on a red rectangle.
mechanism: An opened colon packed with stool illustrates a one-cup, kilos-of-waste claim, with the red block putting the gross-out word at the end of the headline.
composition: Text column on the left half and the intestine graphic on the right, nearly equal weight, with the stool at the lower right as the end point of the read. The graphic's vertical shape fills the full height. The red box is the heaviest block in the text column.
typography: Eight words in four rows: yellow JUST 1 CUP and REMOVES, white KILOS OF, and white on red TOXIC FECES. All rows are readable at 160x90. The title adds the number one and method and the thumbnail adds one cup and toxic.
colors: Black background with yellow and white text, a saturated pink-orange organ and brown lumps, with the red box on TOXIC FECES. The red and yellow act as alarm cues, and the pink-brown contrast makes the stool pop.
psychology: No person or face is shown, so the visible cues are bodily and clinical. The anatomical diagram and the red alarm box give a disgust and urgency tone.
partnership: The title says a number one method flushes kilos of stool and eliminates constipation fast, while the thumbnail names one cup and calls the waste toxic. The overlay therefore escalates the claim and does not say what the cup contains.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow JUST 1 CUP first, then the red TOXIC FECES box, then the stool in the opened colon, then the coiled intestine.
art: Glossy 3D-style organ with segmented bumps and soft highlights, clean against pure black. The organ is anatomically stylised and the lumps are clearly shown, and the elements stay readable at phone size.
strength: Large diagram plus four bold lines make the one-cup claim immediate and legible.
weakness: The claim of kilos of toxic waste is exaggerated and unspecific, and nothing shows what the cup contains.
bottleneck: The remedy itself is absent, so the thumbnail depends on an exaggerated outcome with no concrete ingredient.
action: Hypothesis: replace TOXIC FECES with a neutral word such as STOOL and show a cup in the corner to test whether a concrete object improves clarity without alarm wording.
counterexample: Seq 11 poses a question with real objects and a clinician and makes no outcome claim, the opposite of this absolute outcome claim.
medical_notes: The text claims a single cup removes kilos of toxic feces, with no named remedy, which overstates both the effect and the toxicity.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: SO YOU WANT TO START / A COURIER BUSINESS / Driver Salaries / Package Delivery Revenue / Dispatch & Software / Vehicle Maintenance / Fuel & Tolls / [van livery: FAST TRACK COURIER]
scene: Five hand-drawn red ovals with labels, Driver Salaries, Package Delivery Revenue, Dispatch & Software, Vehicle Maintenance and Fuel & Tolls, surround it, each with a thin black curved arrow; a sixth short unlabelled black arrow points down at the van roof from above.
mechanism: A van annotated like a diagram shows five cost and revenue areas around one business, framing the thumbnail as a whiteboard-style breakdown.
composition: The two-line headline fills the top, the van is the centre, and the five labels ring it in a loose circle. The arrows point inward to create a hub-and-spoke pattern. The red underline separates the headline from the diagram, and the van's size gives a clear focal point.
typography: Nineteen overlay words plus the van's livery: an eight-word two-line headline in heavy black capitals and five small handwritten labels of two to three words each. The headline is readable at 160x90 but the five labels become thin marks. The title says economics, which the labels suggest through cost words.
colors: Black headline and outlines on near-white graph paper, with a white-and-red van and red label ovals as accents. The palette is low in saturation, so the red stripe and ovals are the only warm marks.
psychology: No person appears, so there is no visible expression or gaze. The hand-drawn arrows and ovals give a calm, instructional tone with no fear or urgency cues.
partnership: The title promises economics, and the labels list salaries, revenue, software, maintenance and fuel, which visually previews the breakdown. The headline reads as a how-to opener, while the title is about the economics, so the two have a slightly different angle.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: black headline first, then the van, then the red labels clockwise from the upper left, then the scanner at the lower left.
art: Polished illustration of a van with realistic perspective and shadow, overlaid with hand-drawn style labels. The van's livery text is small but legible in the native image, and the grid background is faint, so it is clean but uses many small parts.
strength: The annotated van gives a clear picture of the business and previews the cost categories.
weakness: Five tiny hand-drawn labels disappear at 160x90, and no person or figure gives the frame an emotional focus.
bottleneck: The economics promise sits entirely in small labels, while the large headline is a generic starter phrase.
action: Hypothesis: keep only two labels, such as Revenue and Fuel & Tolls, at larger size to test whether fewer legible labels convey the economics at phone size.

scene: In a rocky camp, a shaggy-haired stick figure at the left squats with one hand on its head, eyes wide and glancing right, mouth open. Centre-right, a woman figure with two braids and a furrowed brow carries a large stone slab carved with a paw print, zigzags and a tiny stick figure, plus a bundle of sticks, on her back, a long curved tusk trailing behind and a spear in her hand. Behind them are two huts, a small campfire, a pot over a larger fire, four fish hanging on a rack, bones on the ground and three small onlookers.
mechanism: A startled onlooker in the foreground faces a braided woman carrying an oversized stone load, turning the strength question into a visible demonstration.
composition: The squatting figure sits at the left in front and the strong woman is centre-right, forming a reaction-and-subject pair across the middle. The huts, fire and onlookers fill the background at smaller scale. The headline spans the top above the rock peaks, and the busy camp creates a layered depth.
typography: Two words in one line of thick yellow outlined capitals across the top, legible at 160x90. The text uses cavewomen and stronger and omits the title's than we think, leaving the question to the picture.
colors: Warm tan, brown and grey rock tones with a blue sky patch and yellow headline as the brightest element. The orange flames and the pale slab give small warm and light accents against the muted ground.
psychology: The squatting figure has wide eyes, an open mouth and a hand on the head, while the woman has furrowed brows and a level glance. Together the cues show surprise at her load and a determined stance.
partnership: The title asks whether cavewomen were stronger than we think, and the thumbnail shows one carrying a slab, sticks and a tusk. The picture answers visually while the question mark leaves some doubt.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow headline first, then the shocked squatting figure, then the woman with the stone slab, then the campfire and pot on the right.
art: Mixed stick-figure and illustrated-camp style with consistent outlines. The slab with carvings, the tusk and the pot over a fire add clear props, and the background is detailed but muted, so the two main figures stay readable.
strength: A concrete picture of a woman carrying a huge load gives the strength question a direct visual answer.
weakness: The camp background is crowded, with huts, fish, bones and several tiny onlookers competing with the main pair.
bottleneck: Two main figures plus a detailed camp split attention across the frame.
action: Hypothesis: remove the right-hand pot and fish rack and simplify the huts to test whether a cleaner background makes the woman's load stand out more.
counterexample: Seq 15 keeps one large face on flat colour zones, giving an easier phone read than this crowded camp.
